correctness.rationale: For every pair of interior occupancy probabilities and positive rates the loss conditions on first-site occupancy and exact exponential first-detection time. The derivative is the product of a positive factor and a strictly increasing function, giving one global optimal cap. The root identity yields the two-term cap asymptotic. Separating lower-order integration terms produces the exact leading missed-detection coefficient and ratio; the independent integer inequality proves the witness. A standalone script checks the conditional integral via numerical quadrature, derivatives, optimality grids, and both asymptotic orientations; finite tests are supplementary, not an infinite proof. All equal-rate, endpoint-cap and horizon cases are explicitly handled in the proof.

value.rationale: This closes a directly motivated small but complete sequential survey question left outside the expected-budget sitewise ecological model. A hard realized deadline and early time recycling produce a unique cap at every horizon, and the comparative priority index changes from occupancy-times-detection-rate in the short regime to rate-times-log-absence in the long regime. An exact robust parameter example forces a change in optimal visiting order. These features matter as transparent benchmarks for finite-horizon survey planning, even without extending to arbitrary adaptive multistate policies.
